newsitem.title: BELGIUM: E.U. launches probe into sale of Toys 'R' Us Dutch unit.
newsitem.headline: E.U. launches probe into sale of Toys 'R' Us Dutch unit.

text.p: The European Commission said Tuesday it would begin an in-depth antitrust probe into the planned takeover of the Dutch unit of Toys R Us Inc. by Blokker Holding BV.

The European Union executive body said Blokker had by far the largest market share as a toy retailer in the Netherlands and therefore held a "significant position as a retailer and as a purchaser of toys" in the country.

"In assessing the operation, the commission in particular needs to examine the effect of the combination of the Toys 'R Us 'mega' stores with Blokker's familiarity with the Dutch retail market," the commission said in a statement.
"The Commission now has a maximum of a further four months in which to complete its inquiries and take a final decision on the case," it added.
The deal was submitted for clearance by the Dutch authorities. Otherwise, the commission would not have jurisdiction over the operation because it affects mainly the Netherlands.

Toys 'R Us Netherlands is a wholly owned subsidiary of Toys 'R Us Inc of Paramus, N.J., one of the world's biggest toy retailers. It currently operates nine megastores in the Netherlands of which three would be closed if the acquisition were approved, the commission said.
Blokker is a retail chain mainly active in household articles, toys and other products.
